label: D1 after reaching S2, when the agent is about to choose a1
explanation: Fires only at D1 (never GO or D2), at about 17% of D1 steps. It is strongest when the previous trial reached S2 and the agent then picks a1. Top examples are D1 after an unrewarded S2 visit: a2->S2 common, unrewarded (switch to a1), or a1->S2 rare, unrewarded (stay with a1). Both are model-based signs that S2 is bad and a1 is the better choice. Adding prev_reward==0 gives precision 0.92 but loses recall, so I dropped it. The predicate uses the upcoming GO choice (action), which is marked FUTURE but is the agent computing its own choice, not a random outcome. The closest predicate using only observed variables, D1 & prev_state==2 & prev_reward==0, scores P 0.61 R 0.54 F1 0.57 on dev, and D1 & prev_state==2 alone reaches mass recall 0.84 but precision 0.35. Recall is limited: about 16% of the activation mass is at the window D1 of rel -3, where the previous trial lies outside the window. The other misses are mostly weak activations. Magnitude is higher when the previous trial was unrewarded (rate 0.11 vs 0.03 when rewarded), when value is low, and late in the episode (trials 90-99). It does not fire at GO or D2, after an S1 visit followed by a1, or when the agent is about to choose a2 after an S2 reward.
